feedback.end: In the mid 1800s, the scientist Charles Darwin created the theory of evolution, which explains how living things have changed over time.
When Charles Darwin went to the Galapagos Islands in South America, he observed differences between animals that led him to create his theory of evolution.

instruction.text: You are talking to Charles Darwin. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: What did you observe on the ((++Galapagos Falkland)) Islands?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.75st'>What did you observe on the Galapagos Islands?</prosody>

atoms.b: I noticed that there were ((++animals buildings)) on the different islands that looked very similar. However, when I looked closer, I saw that there were also clear ((++differences colours)) between these animals.
One animal that I observed was the ((++tortoise dinosaur)). I noticed that tortoises on the different islands had different shaped shells.
How did this lead to your theory of ((++evolution destruction))?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.75st'>How did this lead to your theory of evolution?</prosody>

atoms.b: I theorised that these animals must have looked the same in the ((++past future)) but changed over time to better suit the ((++environment sky)) of their specific island. This made me believe that all living things have evolved over time.

instruction.text: Darwin also observed differences between a species of bird called finches. Select the bird with the correct feature.

feedback.end: Finches with long, thin beaks live on islands with lots of tiny insects to eat.
Finches with wide, blunt beaks use them to crush the nuts and seeds available on their island.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Why do finches have different beaks?

b.sound: Their beaks have adapted according to the food available in their environment.

feedback.end: Darwin theorised that these finches all looked the same in the past. However, as they settled in different areas over time, their features adapted to help them in their environment.
